   "source": [
    "# Marching Cubes\n",
    "\n",
    "Marching cubes is the workhorse of iso-surface extraction: it visits\n",
    "every grid cell and cuts triangles out of it based on which corners\n",
    "are inside the surface. It is the default choice for most fields.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-07T06:38:55.126993Z",

     "iopub.status.idle": "2026-07-07T06:38:55.990495Z",
     "shell.execute_reply": "2026-07-07T06:38:55.990053Z"
    }

   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import torch\n",
    "import isoext\n",
    "from isoext import viewer\n",
    "\n",
    "# Setup: create a grid with a sphere\n",
    "grid = isoext.UniformGrid([64, 64, 64])\n",
    "points = grid.get_points()\n",
    "grid.set_values(points.norm(dim=-1) - 0.7)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Basic Usage\n",
    "\n",
    "```python\n",
    "vertices, faces = isoext.marching_cubes(grid, level=0.0, method=\"vega\")\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "- `grid`: A `UniformGrid` or `SparseGrid` with values set\n",
    "- `level`: The iso-value to extract (default: 0.0)\n",
    "- `method`: Algorithm variant (`\"vega\"`, `\"lewiner\"`, `\"nagae\"`, or `\"lorensen\"`)\n"
   ]
  },

    "print(f\"Faces: {faces.shape}\")  # (M, 3) uint32\n",
    "\n",
    "viewer.embed(vertices, faces)"

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## How It Works\n",
    "\n",
    "Marching cubes visits every cell independently. Each of a cell's 8\n",
    "corners is either inside or outside the surface, giving 256 possible\n",
    "sign patterns, and a lookup table maps each pattern to a set of\n",
    "triangles. The triangle vertices sit on the cell's edges. If one end of an\n",
    "edge is inside the surface and the other is outside, the surface has\n",
    "to cross that edge somewhere in between, and interpolating the two\n",
    "values estimates where: with level-relative endpoint values $v_a$\n",
    "and $v_b$, the crossing sits at the fraction $t = v_a / (v_a - v_b)$\n",
    "of the way along the edge. An endpoint whose value is close to zero\n",
    "is close to the surface, so it pulls the crossing toward itself.\n",
    "\n",
    "The simplest pattern has one corner inside, the red dot below. The\n",
    "surface crosses the three edges that connect it to outside corners;\n",
    "the gold dots mark those crossings. For this pattern the lookup\n",
    "table produces one triangle, and the three crossings are its\n",
    "vertices:\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-07T06:38:56.066600Z",

    "cell = isoext.UniformGrid([2, 2, 2])\n",
    "cell.set_values(torch.tensor(\n",
    "    [-0.5, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2], device=\"cuda\"\n",
    ").reshape(2, 2, 2))\n",
    "\n",
    "crossings = isoext.get_intersection(cell).get_points()\n",
    "v, f = isoext.marching_cubes(cell)\n",
    "print(f\"{f.shape[0]} triangle(s)\")\n",
    "viewer.embed(v, f, color=\"steelblue\", flat_shading=True, side=\"double\", height=300,\n",
    "             grid=cell, draw=lambda s: viewer.add_points(s, crossings, point_size=0.09))\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Algorithm Variants\n",
    "\n",
    "The `method` argument selects between four variants that share the\n",
    "same interface:\n",
    "\n",
    "- `vega` (default) resolves topological ambiguities by following the\n",
    "  field's interpolant, using the corrected interior test.\n",
    "- `lewiner` follows the interpolant with the older interior test;\n",
    "  kept for comparison with other implementations.\n",
    "- `nagae` uses fixed tables; always closed and slightly faster.\n",
    "- `lorensen` is the original 1987 algorithm; ambiguous cells can\n",
    "  leave small cracks.\n",
    "\n",
    "See {doc}`mc_variants` for the differences in detail.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,

    "    v, f = isoext.marching_cubes(grid, method=method)\n",
    "    print(f\"{method:9s} {f.shape[0]:,} triangles\")"
   ]

   "source": [
    "## Iso-Level\n",
    "\n",
    "The `level` parameter controls which iso-surface to extract. For signed distance fields, `level=0` gives the surface. Other values give offset surfaces:\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "metadata": {
    "execution": {
     "iopub.execute_input": "2026-07-07T06:38:56.161797Z",

     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "level=-0.2: 4,728 vertices (radius ≈ 0.9)\n",
      "level=+0.0: 9,168 vertices (radius ≈ 0.7)\n",
      "level=+0.2: 15,072 vertices (radius ≈ 0.5)\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# Extract at different iso-levels\n",
    "for level in [-0.2, 0.0, 0.2]:\n",
    "    v, f = isoext.marching_cubes(grid, level=level)\n",
    "    print(f\"level={level:+.1f}: {v.shape[0]:,} vertices (radius ≈ {0.7 - level:.1f})\")"
   ]
  },

    "\n",

    "print(\"Saved to mesh.obj\")"
